answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust grow like a pearl: each identity starts as a bare grain of sand and earns thin nacre layers only through verified work, so a fresh fake has nothing to spend. Work histories live on separate island ledgers, and moving between islands needs a sponsor who stakes reputation on the newcomer. Records settle into shale strata that fingerprint the tools and tasks behind them, so two identities sharing one stratum are exposed as one actor, fused together, and both lose their stake. Cheap copies stay worthless while real work compounds.
